_what: The delivery graph's declared intent: which master each act's Prod/ entry hardlinks, and which acts have no social copy ON PURPOSE. tools/deliver.py reads this beside docs/running-order.md (which stays the source of truth for the act list and its ORDER -- this file is keyed by act numeral and says nothing about order). A master path is `~`-rooted or absolute, never relative to a worktree: worktrees are ephemeral, and act II's link into dv-wt/feat-98-act2-overlay is the recorded hazard. When a project's build replaces its master as a NEW inode (tools/peaks.py trim does os.replace on purpose), the Prod link is detached and `deliver.py publish` re-links it -- that re-link is the step peaks.py deliberately does not do.
_rules: publish re-links only when the declared master is NEWER than what Prod carries, or when the content is identical (re-attaching is then free). A declared master that is OLDER than Prod's current content is a conflict -- reported, never force-linked: something built Prod's content and the master never received it (act II on 2026-08-13: the #98 build lived only in a worktree while the main checkout's renders/efmb-plated.mp4 was a revision behind; repaired under #150 by promoting the worktree build onto the durable master). A master path that resolves inside a git worktree is EPHEMERAL and publish refuses to link from it at any mtime -- promote it to a durable path first. FOOTAGE is declared by video_id, never by path: media/ is gitignored, so the picture an act was cut from is invisible to `sources`, and a master that changes container (.mp4 -> .mkv, #229) must still resolve. tools/footage.py resolves an id to its file and hashes it, cached by (path, size, mtime_ns). An act with no `footage` key is UNDECLARED and reported, never assumed fresh.

_sources: `sources` is the rung BEFORE the master: the committed inputs an act is built from. tools/deliver.py hashes them and compares against `source_digest`, which `publish` stamps -- so editing a shotlist, a plate manifest, a dialogue record or vocab/casting.yaml marks that act's delivered film STALE instead of letting it silently predate its own inputs. Content hashed, never mtime: these come out of git, where every mtime is checkout time. An empty list means the act has no committed inputs AT ALL and its note must say so -- that is a finding, not a configuration. An act with no `sources` key is reported UNDECLARED so nobody mistakes silence for freshness.
